What happens to f(n) as n increases?
f(n) = |(5 – 6i)"|
A. As n increases, f(n) remains constant.
B. As n increases, f(n) increases.
C. As n increases, f(n) decreases.
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 correctly applies the modulus property |(5−6i)^n| = |5−6i|^n = (√61)^n, concluding that f(n) increases as n grows (option B). Candidate 2 incorrectly argues the expression stays constant by treating the base’s absolute value as making the whole power independent of n. Candidate 3 gives an incorrect constant value f(n)=1 by effectively omitting the necessary factor (√61)^n in the polar-form magnitude. Candidate 4 similarly claims constancy after noting |(5−6i)^n| = |5−6i|^n, which is not constant for n>0.
